sections.body: A fair test changes ONE thing (the variable you test) and keeps everything else the same.
Decide what you MEASURE, then record results in a table.
Repeat the test to make sure results are reliable, then write a CONCLUSION: what did you find out?
Example: Does sugar dissolve faster in hot water? Change only the water temperature. Same amount of sugar, same cup, same stirring.

quiz.q: Testing whether plants grow taller with more light, what must you keep the same?
hints: Testing which paper towel is most absorbent: same water, same size towel. Only the brand changes.
quiz.explain: Keep water, soil and plant type the same, and only change the light.

options: To check the results are reliable
Because the first one was boring
hints: Could one result be a fluke?
Doing it again checks if you get similar results.
If you flip a coin once and get heads, does that prove coins always land heads?
quiz.explain: Repeating checks your results weren't a one-off fluke.
